question.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $y,$ so we will treat the other variables $w,x,$ and $z$ as constants. We can use the addition and multiplication principles to solve for $y.$

First, we subtract $2xz$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}2xz-3y & =4w \\ 2xz-3y-2xz & =4w-2xz \\ -3y & =4w-2xz\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide by $-3$ to get $y$ alone:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3y & =4w-2xz \\ \frac{-3y}{-3} & =\frac{4w-2xz}{-3} \\ y & =\frac{4w-2xz}{-3} \\ y & =\frac{2xz-4w}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
